Resolve the mechanics decisions with these defaults: use the normal third-person Roblox camera, keep the target dummy fixed in place, and keep a session-only hit counter with no reset button. Every accepted punch on the dummy increments it once. These settle the three open mechanics questions.

Preview an animation clip
Punch Trainer: Target Dummy Arena

Saved proposal · revision 3

Mechanics

Core loop: Player character stands in a small arena facing a stationary Target Dummy, viewed through the standard Roblox third-person follow camera (default over-the-shoulder perspective, player-controlled via standard WASD movement and camera orbit). Pressing the punch input (default: left mouse click / gamepad X / keyboard F) triggers a punch animation on the player rig. On animation hit-frame, a hit-detection check (overlap/raycast from fist socket) determines if the dummy is within range. On successful hit: (1) play punch VFX (impact particle burst at contact point), (2) play punch SFX (whoosh + impact sound layered), (3) play dummy reaction (small knockback/flinch animation or physics impulse), (4) increment a session-only Hit Counter UI element by exactly 1 per accepted punch, (5) briefly flash/scale the counter text for feedback. The Target Dummy is permanently fixed in its spawn position for the session — it does not move, respawn, or reposition, and only visually reacts (flinch/impulse) to hits while staying rooted in place. The Hit Counter has no reset button or reset key; it counts up indefinitely for the duration of the play session and only clears on scene/session reload. Dummy has a fixed hitbox volume; no health/death state in this default scope (pure hit-tracking, not damage/KO). Punch has a short cooldown/animation-lock (~0.4s) to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per swing. Whiff (miss) attempts play swing SFX/VFX only, no counter increment. Optional combo window not included by default (single punch type only) to keep scope minimal.

Assumptions: Single punch type (no combo strings, kicks, or special moves) unless expanded later. Dummy is stationary and does not fight back, block, or die — it's a practice target, not an opponent. Dummy position is permanently fixed for the session; no respawn or repositioning logic is included. Hit Counter is session-only (no reset button/key) and resets only on scene/session reload; no persistent save-across-sessions system unless requested. Camera is the standard Roblox default third-person follow camera; no custom camera rig or first-person/2D mode. One player-controlled character; no multiplayer/versus mode included. Hit detection uses a simple overlap/trigger volume on the dummy rather than full physics-based collision resolution. VFX and SFX are single default punch impact assets (no combo-dependent variation) unless marketplace assets specify otherwise. No damage numbers, health bars, or dummy destruction — scope is strictly a hit-counting trainer.

Theme

A minimal, clean training-gym aesthetic centered on a single practice dummy and a player character in a combat stance, now bathed in a cool blue-lit atmosphere. The space reads as a modern dojo/gym bay lit primarily by blue-toned fixtures (e.g., cool blue overhead panels, rim lighting, or accent strips along the walls/floor), casting a focused blue glow on the dummy and player. Visual tone remains functional and readable over stylized — the priority is clear feedback (impact VFX, snappy animation, satisfying counter tick) rather than narrative or world-building. Think a late-night training bay vibe: neutral gray/dark surfaces contrasted by blue ambient and key lighting, with punchy, arcade-like impact effects (small spark/dust burst, brief screen feedback) that pop against the cool-toned backdrop to make each hit feel rewarding.

Assumptions: No story, characters beyond the player and dummy, or narrative framing — this is a mechanics/skill-training sandbox. Punch VFX styled as simple impact bursts (dust/spark particles) rather than exaggerated anime-style energy effects, unless otherwise specified. SFX styled as realistic-ish punch/impact sounds (thud, whoosh) rather than cartoonish or sci-fi styled sounds. Player character appearance/model is a placeholder/generic fighter rig unless specific character assets are requested. Blue lighting is achieved via lighting/color-grading (cool blue key/ambient lights, blue accent fixtures) rather than changing overall environment geometry or layout. Base surfaces (floor, walls) remain neutral gray/dark tones so the blue lighting reads clearly as the dominant color cue.

Environment & layout

Single small enclosed arena/room representing a training space (e.g., a gym floor or dojo mat). Layout: player spawns at a fixed position facing the Target Dummy, which is placed a short, fixed punching-range distance away and remains permanently rooted in that spot for the session. Hit Counter UI is docked in a fixed screen position (e.g., top-center or top-right) for constant visibility during practice, with no reset control present on-screen. Minimal environment dressing — a floor, simple wall/backdrop, and basic ambient lighting — to keep focus on the player-dummy interaction, viewed via the standard Roblox third-person camera. No additional NPCs, hazards, or secondary objects in this default scope.

Assumptions: Static single-room environment; no level progression, multiple arenas, or exploration space. Dummy position is fixed at scene start and does not move during gameplay (only reacts with hit animation/impulse), consistent with the resolved mechanics decision. Lighting is simple and functional (e.g., single directional/ambient setup) rather than dramatic or scene-specific. Environment scale is small (single room, walking-distance interaction) rather than open-world.
